newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issues to pick up, players eye rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issues to pick up, players eye rates.

text.p: As U.S. corporations approach the end of the year end, many are expected to wrap up any financing needs now while a favorable interest rate environment prevails, dealers said.
"It's a positive issuing environment," said one syndicate official. "I suspect there's going to be a lot of issuance in the next few weeks."

Lower financing rates and a rapidly approaching end to the calendar year should push issuance to the forefront now as upcoming holidays, coupled with thinly staffed desks, make it difficult to structure new deals.
"If you're thinking about issuing debt you may as well do it now," said another syndicate source. "It starts getting tough toward year-end when you have all these holidays coming up."

In upcoming high-grade issues, Smith Barney Holdings is expected to tap the market with $200 million in A2/A-minus rated 10-year debt. Price talk on the issue is 68 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, syndicate sources said.
Allegiance Healthcare is expected to tap the market with $500 million in a three-part debt offering via Goldman Sachs.
"Issuance may start off a little slow, but it will definitely pick up at these levels," one dealer said.
Among high-yield issuers expected to tap the markets are the following, dealers said:
Goss Graphic Systems $225 million in B2/B-rated senior subordianted notes due 2006 via CS First Boston.
Paging Network Inc is expected to price $350 million in B2/B rated 144A senior subordinated notes due 2008 via Goldamn Sachs.
In foreign issues, Banco Santander is expected to price $150 million in 10-year subordinated yankee notes.
Brazil is also expected to tap the market with a five-year or ten-year global issue, sources said.
In the government market, the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond is off 8/32 at 99-23/32 to yield 6.77 percent.
